To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the expression of Cx43 is reduced in ischemic myocardium, (2) the reduction of Cx43 expression in the myocardium is associated with a reduction in the conduction velocity, and (3) the reduction of conduction velocity is associated with the induction of ventricular tachyfibrillation.

connexin 43 is the major gap junction protein in the ventricular myocyte, and connexin 45 is a gap junction protein in ventricular myocytes, but it is localized in the lateral membrane of the myocyte, and is not involved in electrical coupling.
the induction of arrhythmia is related to the expression of the connexin 43 (Cx43) protein in the myocardium.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular basis of cardiac electrical activity and its alteration by myocardial ischemia.
the molecular mechanisms of arrhythmia.
the mechanisms of arrhythmogenesis in the heart and the role of connexins in this process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
connexin 43, a protein that forms gap junctions between cardiomyocytes, is an important determinant of the conduction properties of the heart, and its expression is altered by ischemic conditions.

the connexin 43 protein plays an important role in the genesis of arrhythmias, especially in ischemia-induced arrhythmias, but the exact mechanisms of its involvement in arrhythmogenesis have yet to be elucidated.
connexin channels are not the sole determinants of slow conduction, but they play an important role in this process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the electrical conduction system of the heart is a complex network of specialized cells that are interconnected by gap junctions.

we have shown that the expression of the gap junction proteins, connexin 40, 43, and 45, are downregulated in the ischemic region of the heart, and that the downregulation of connexin 45 is associated with an increased incidence of reentrant arrhythmias.
we have shown that the connexin43 gene is a candidate gene for arrhythmogenicity and that connexins may play a role in the development of cardiac arrhythmias.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the gap junctions in the ventricles are more susceptible to ischemia-induced uncoupling than those in the atria.
